clue.text: She received her own thimble as her prize

definitions.text: She received her own thimble as her prize

parts.words: She received her own thimble as her prize
parts.note: in Lewis Carroll's Wonderland, after the Caucus-race the Dodo takes the heroine's thimble from her and solemnly presents it back to her as her prize

explanation.walkthrough: A pure cryptic definition: the solver needs to recall the Caucus-race scene in Alice's Adventures in Wonderland.
explanation.definitionFit: The girl in Carroll's story is the one who is handed back her own sewing thimble as the reward for the race.

clue.text: BR order to get out balance of payments in full

definitions.meaning: British Rail guards called this when everyone must leave the train at the end of the line
change is the balance handed back when paying, and all means in full

explanation.walkthrough: BR is British Rail, the former national railway; 'balance of payments' is not economics but the change from a purchase.
explanation.definitionFit: The railway call tells passengers to leave the train, and it also means every bit of the money returned after paying.

clue.text: Solid gold piece entered in part exchange

indicators.note: the two parts of the phrase for entered swap places

parts.note: got in means entered

explanation.surface: A gold bar handed over as part of a trade-in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part exchange' is a trade-in, but here it means GOT and IN swap places.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar of cast metal, especially gold, is a solid lump of the precious metal.

clue.text: Jewellery items are removed, doctor, before operations

indicators.note: removed suggests the letters of are are moved around into a new order

parts.note: ops is short for operations

explanation.surface: Patients' jewellery is taken off by the doctor before surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removed' is the anagram signal, though the surface makes it sound like taking jewellery off before surgery.
explanation.definitionFit: These are earrings with hanging pendants, pieces of jewellery worn on the lobes.

clue.text: Conveyance from race in which I led before river turn

indicators.note: the race is a container: I sits inside its two letters

parts.note: the TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man
taken as written

indicators.note: turn tells us the river's name is read backwards here

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and on the English-Welsh border

explanation.surface: A conveyancing document somehow tied to a race the speaker led until reaching a river bend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conveyance' is the legal transfer of property, not transport; 'turn' reverses the river and 'before' only sets the order.
explanation.definitionFit: In law a conveyance is the deed transferring ownership of land, the paper proof of title.

clue.text: It's up to the old war leader

indicators.note: up in a down clue tells us the word it is read from bottom to top

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A remark that it falls to a former military chief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns IT round in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Josip Broz led the Yugoslav partisans in the Second World War and later ruled Yugoslavia.

clue.text: Man of conviction or a trimmer? Paper always about right

definitions.text: Man of conviction or a trimmer

parts.note: The Times is the newspaper

indicators.note: about means the word for always goes round the abbreviation for right

parts.note: ever means always

explanation.surface: A principled man or an opportunist? The newspaper is always on the right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man of conviction' is a convict serving time; a trimmer is someone who shifts opinions to suit the times.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a prisoner doing a sentence and an opportunist who bends to current fashion fit this word.

clue.text: This inventor in turn announces end of play

indicators.note: in turn means the call is read backwards

parts.note: no side is what a rugby referee calls at the end of a match

explanation.surface: An inventor who takes his turn to say the game is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No side' is the old rugby term for the final whistle, unfamiliar outside rugby countries.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Alva Edison was the American inventor of the phonograph and a practical light bulb.

clue.text: Questioning test in analysis of gin

parts.note: an exam is a test
taken as written

indicators.note: analysis breaks the word gin up so its letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Checking a test result in a laboratory study of gin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'analysis of' rearranges GIN to ING.
explanation.definitionFit: Questioning someone closely is cross-examination, interrogating them.

clue.text: Funny Girl (for Guy) seen around the river

indicators.note: seen around means the girl's word wraps round the abbreviation for river

parts.note: doll is slang for a girl, as in the musical Guys and Dolls

explanation.surface: A comic girl spotted near the river with her boyfriend Guy.
explanation.walkthrough: '(for Guy)' points to Guys and Dolls, where the women are dolls.
explanation.definitionFit: Droll describes humour that is dry and quietly amusing.

clue.text: To get right loam mixture use this computer aid

indicators.note: a mixture of the letters means the two words are stirred together into a new order

explanation.surface: Advice on blending soil correctly with a calculating tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixture' rearranges RIGHT and LOAM; 'computer' means one who computes, in the old sense of calculating by hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Before calculators, tables of these exponents were the standard aid for anyone doing long multiplication by hand.

clue.text: Vanessa perhaps makes mark in Shakespearian role

indicators.note: in places the mark inside the role's name

parts.note: Iago is the villain in Othello
M is short for the German mark, the old currency

explanation.surface: An actress called Vanessa scores a hit playing a Shakespeare part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vanessa' suggests an actress such as Vanessa Redgrave, but it is a genus of butterflies, such as the red admiral.
explanation.definitionFit: Vanessa is a butterfly genus, and an adult butterfly is the final, winged stage of an insect's life.

clue.text: They detest madmen, proverbially heartless

indicators.note: heartless asks us to drop the central letter of the word for madmen

parts.note: the saying 'mad as a hatter' makes hat-makers the proverbial madmen

explanation.surface: People who loathe lunatics, known for having no feelings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes one of the two middle Ts from HATTERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who detest something are people who loathe it, a noun for those holding hostility.

clue.text: Spain's tourist attraction converted into calories

indicators.note: converted means the letters of calories are changed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A Spanish sight being turned into dietary energy.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of CALORIES is the royal palace-monastery near Madrid.
explanation.definitionFit: The palace and monastery complex built by Philip II outside Madrid draws many visitors.

clue.text: He prevents enjoyment of booty left on board

parts.note: spoils are loot or booty
port is the left-hand side of a ship

explanation.surface: A man stopping the fun over loot left on a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' means aboard a ship, where left is port.
explanation.definitionFit: A killjoy is someone who ruins others' fun.

clue.text: Jupiter was one of those known in Barchester

definitions.text: Jupiter was one of those known in Barchester

parts.words: Jupiter was one of those known in Barchester
parts.note: in Trollope's Barchester novels the Jupiter is a thinly disguised version of The Times, a daily paper, not the god or planet

explanation.walkthrough: Jupiter looks like the planet or the Roman god; Trollope used the name for his fictional London daily.
explanation.definitionFit: The Jupiter was one of the daily journals read in Trollope's fictional cathedral city.

clue.text: One lent its name to the Arrowmaker's daughter

definitions.text: One lent its name to the Arrowmaker's daughter

parts.words: One lent its name to the Arrowmaker's daughter
parts.note: in Longfellow's Hiawatha the arrow-maker's daughter is Minnehaha, Laughing Water, named after a cascade

explanation.walkthrough: Minnehaha is said to mean laughing water, and Minnehaha Falls in Minneapolis carries the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Minnehaha takes her name from a cascade of laughing water.

clue.text: Friendly type

explanation.definitionFit: Kind can be an adjective for warm and considerate, or a noun for a sort or category.

clue.text: Run down, dear, and get in somehow

indicators.note: somehow says the letters of dear and get in are arranged in some other way

explanation.surface: Sneering at someone dear, and getting in anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run down' looks like physical exhaustion; it means belittle.
explanation.definitionFit: To belittle or disparage someone is to criticise them unfairly.

clue.text: Lover is married. I emphasize

parts.note: to stress is to emphasize

explanation.surface: A declaration that a lover has a spouse, with emphasis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' links definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman in a sexual relationship with a married man is his kept lover.

clue.text: One who painted Elizabeth topless

indicators.note: topless removes the first letter of the pet name

parts.note: Betty is a pet form of the name Elizabeth

explanation.surface: An artist who portrayed a woman named Elizabeth without her top on.
explanation.walkthrough: William Etty was a Victorian painter famous for nudes, which makes 'topless' doubly apt.
explanation.definitionFit: William Etty was a nineteenth-century English artist known for his nude figures.

clue.text: She was well-oiled at the reception!

definitions.text: She was well-oiled at the reception!

parts.words: She was well-oiled at the reception!
parts.note: well-oiled suggests drunk at a party, but in the parable of the ten virgins the prudent ones brought spare oil for their lamps and were let in to the wedding feast

explanation.walkthrough: 'well-oiled' is British slang for drunk; here it means supplied with lamp oil, from Matthew 25.
explanation.definitionFit: In Jesus's parable the prudent bridesmaids kept their lamps filled and went in to the marriage feast.

clue.text: Put forward tricky legal point

indicators.note: tricky suggests the letters of legal are handled in a twisty way

parts.note: E is a compass point, east

explanation.surface: Raising a difficult point of law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tricky' rearranges LEGAL into ALLEG; 'point' is the compass point E.
explanation.definitionFit: To claim something without proof is to assert it.

clue.text: Indifferent Sheridan character couldn't do this?

definitions.meaning: one of the dissolute young men in Sheridan's play The School for Scandal

explanation.walkthrough: 'couldn't do this?' hints at 'couldn't care less', the idiom for indifference.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means unconcerned, and the name belongs to a rakish friend of Charles Surface in The School for Scandal.

clue.text: Press Charles the First to meet the parliamentarian

parts.note: CR is Carolus Rex, King Charles
I is the Roman numeral one
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Push King Charles I to confront a member of Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charles the First' looks like one piece, but splits into CR and I.
explanation.definitionFit: To crimp is to press into small folds or ridges.

clue.text: The way a convict adapts to prison in Germany

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way
lag is British slang for a convict, as in 'old lag'

explanation.surface: How a prisoner gets used to life in a German jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adapts to' is only a link here, and 'prison in Germany' recalls the German camps for prisoners of war.
explanation.definitionFit: German camps for prisoners of war in the Second World War were called by this German word.

clue.text: Turner has health ruined by hospital omission

indicators.note: ruined says the letters of health are wrecked and reassembled
omission means the hospital letter is left out

explanation.surface: An artist named Turner has his health wrecked by a hospital's neglect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turner' is not the painter but a machine that turns wood or metal; 'ruined' rearranges HEALTH and 'omission' leaves out the H for hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that spins a workpiece for shaping is a turning tool.

clue.text: … from cliff and ——The horns of Elfland" (Tennyson)

definitions.text: … from cliff and ——The horns of Elfland" (Tennyson)

parts.words: … from cliff and ——The horns of Elfland" (Tennyson)
parts.note: fill the gap in Tennyson's song from The Princess: 'O sweet and far from cliff and ___ / The horns of Elfland faintly blowing'

explanation.walkthrough: A quotation clue; the missing word is also a crag, a steep rock face.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word names a steep rocky outcrop, which sits naturally beside cliff in the line.

clue.text: Furious at loss of opening for plunder

indicators.note: loss of opening means the first letter of the word for plunder is dropped

parts.note: to pirate is to plunder or rob, especially at sea

explanation.surface: Someone enraged at failing to get the chance to loot.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the P from PIRATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Furious means extremely angry, and so does the answer, from Latin for anger.

clue.text: Players have strong-box with odd Scottish binding

indicators.note: binding means the Scots word is wrapped around the box

parts.note: orra is a Scots word meaning odd or occasional
a chest is a box for keeping valuables

explanation.surface: Musicians own a safe with a strange Scottish wrapping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'binding' is the container signal; the Scots word is split by the box, which sits between its first two and last two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Players here are musicians, and a large body of them performing together is this ensemble.

clue.text: Synthetic material by the Misses Peachum and Waters, say

indicators.note: say tells us that the two first names, run together, are heard rather than spelt

parts.note: Polly Peachum is the heroine of Gay's The Beggar's Opera, and Esther Waters is the title character of George Moore's novel

explanation.surface: A man-made fabric supplied by two literary heroines.
explanation.walkthrough: Polly plus Esther said aloud gives the fabric's name.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a man-made fibre spun from plastic, widely used in clothing.

clue.text: The craft of the Jumblies

parts.note: in Edward Lear's nonsense poem the Jumblies went to sea in a kitchen utensil full of holes

explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' means a boat here, not skill: Lear's poem says 'They went to sea in a Sieve, they did'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Lear's poem the boat the Jumblies sailed in was a strainer full of holes.
